Subject: ZenHealth POC kickoff recap & next steps

Hi Jordan + team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great kickoff. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the proposed scope for the 6-week POC, success metrics, owners, and immediate access/setup steps so we can get started next week.

Pain points we heard
- Clinicians spend ~6-8 minutes per patient chart summarizing notes into the post-visit summary; this is the top manual bottleneck.
- Inconsistent patient instructions across care teams leads to follow-up questions and avoidable calls.
- Current on-prem solution has poor latency and high TCO for nightly batch tasks.

Primary goals for the POC
1) Reduce clinician summarization time by 40% (time-per-chart)
2) Improve first-pass accuracy of patient instructions (measured by internal eval set and clinician QA)
3) Demonstrate <500ms median inference latency for single-message summarization requests in the pilot environment

Proposed POC scope (6 weeks)
- Week 0: Access & infra setup (AWS cross-account role + S3 sample drop)
- Weeks 1-2: Prompt set & eval creation (10k de-identified notes sample; establish evaluation rubric)
- Weeks 3-4: Integration + throughput tuning (batching/kv caching configs, quantization tests)
- Week 5: Internal clinician review / quality check (cohort of 10 clinicians)
- Week 6: Wrap-up & success review; handoff + recommended configs for production

Success metrics (primary)
- Time-per-chart reduction target: 40% (baseline collected by ZenHealth analytics)
- Quality: >= 85% pass rate on clinician QA rubric and parity on instructions accuracy vs. baseline
- Latency: median <500ms for single requests in pilot infra

Owners
- ZenHealth: Jordan Lee (Product), Priya Sharma (Clinical ops), Samir Patel (SRE)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Engg lead / Sales PM), Aditya Rao (Tech lead - infra & deployment), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions / Eval lead)

Immediate access / setup items (actions for this week)
1) ZenHealth: drop 1,000 de-identified sample notes to the S3 bucket we discussed (prefix: zenhealth/poc/samples) OR share a temporary SFTP; include a small README with column schema — owner: Priya — due Tue 2026-03-03
2) ZenHealth: Create an IAM role for cross-account access and send the Role ARN to aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com — owner: Samir — due Wed 2026-03-04
3) Redwood: Share MoP (scope doc) and initial prompt set + eval template — owner: Marissa — attached (zenhealth_poc_mop_v1.pdf) and prompt CSV (zenhealth_prompt_set_v1.csv)
4) Schedule weekly sync: propose Thursdays 10am PT starting 2026-03-05 (will send calendar invite)

Risks / open questions
- We need confirmation on whether PHI will be allowed in the sample bucket (if yes, we will require encryption & KMS + SOC2 attestation).
- Are there any regulatory constraints that prevent sharing de-identified notes outside your VPC?

Next steps (by me)
- Send calendar invite for recurring sync (Thu 10am PT)
- Share technical checklist + small-run test plan after we confirm the role ARN

Attachments: zenhealth_poc_mop_v1.pdf, zenhealth_prompt_set_v1.csv
Doc link: https://drive.google.com/zenhealth-poc-plan

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Quick replies inline: 

- Confirmed: we'll aim to drop 1,000 de-identified notes by Tue (Priya is coordinating).
- For PHI: we will not include PHI in the initial sample set. For later phases we may need a VPC-restricted flow; we'll surface that during week 3.
- IAM role: Samir will create the cross-account role and send the ARN by Wednesday. He flagged that ZenHealth requires an explicit SCP/permission boundary; I'll loop him in.

A couple of asks from our side:
1) Can you include a short SOC2 overview and our standard DPA language? Our procurement team will need that by next week.
2) On latency: our internal threshold for interactive clinician workflows is 300ms median — is that feasible for the single-message path in the pilot infra or should we treat 300ms as stretch?

We're aligned on owners. Please go ahead and send the recurring calendar invite for Thu 10am PT.
